name: Kurdish Macrolanguage

formality.description: Kurdish varieties have T-V pronominal distinctions: Kurmanji tu/hûn, Sorani to/êwe. Formal address uses plural pronouns for singular referents. Formality is also expressed through vocabulary choice and discourse particles. The system is similar across varieties despite script and structural differences.

gender.inclusiveGuidance: Gender varies WITHIN the macrolanguage: Kurmanji (Northern Kurdish) retains a full masculine/feminine gender system with agreement on articles, adjectives, and verbs. Sorani (Central Kurdish) has LOST grammatical gender — no gender agreement, gender-neutral pronouns. This is a fundamental structural difference between the two main varieties. Cards for individual varieties MUST override this field.

linguisticChallenges.scriptSplit: Kurdish varieties use different scripts: Kurmanji (Northern Kurdish) uses Latin script (Hawar alphabet, LTR) in Turkey and Syria. Sorani (Central Kurdish) uses modified Arabic/Persian script (RTL) in Iraq and Iran. This is NOT just a transliteration difference — orthographic conventions, word boundaries, and even morphological representation differ by script. MT must handle both scripts correctly.
linguisticChallenges.splitErgativity: Both major Kurdish varieties exhibit split ergativity — ergative-absolutive alignment in past tenses (the agent of a past transitive verb takes oblique case) and nominative-accusative in present tenses. The ergative split is more prominent in Kurmanji than Sorani.
linguisticChallenges.ezafeConstruction: Both varieties use the ezāfe construction (Kurmanji -a/-ê/-ên, Sorani -î/-y) to link nouns to modifiers, shared with Persian. Ezāfe forms differ by variety and interact with gender (in Kurmanji) and definiteness.
linguisticChallenges.genderAsymmetry: Kurmanji's full M/F gender system vs. Sorani's genderless system is the most dramatic structural difference within a single macrolanguage. MT systems must apply completely different agreement rules depending on the target variety.
linguisticChallenges.lightVerbs: Both varieties use light verb constructions shared with the Iranian genus: noun/adjective + light verb (kirin 'to do', bûn 'to become', dan 'to give', etc.). Compound verb inventories differ between Kurmanji and Sorani.
linguisticChallenges.dialectContinuum: Kurdish forms a dialect continuum — Kurmanji, Sorani, and Southern Kurdish (Kelhuri/Feyli) grade into each other geographically. Written standards exist for Kurmanji and Sorani but are not fully standardized. Vocabulary, morphology, and syntax all show continuous variation.

notes: Macrolanguage card for Kurdish (kur). Covers Kurmanji/Northern Kurdish (kmr, Latin script), Sorani/Central Kurdish (ckb, Arabic script), and Southern Kurdish (sdh). Script and direction are null because of the Latin (LTR)/Arabic (RTL) split. Gender is null because Kurmanji has it and Sorani doesn't. Individual variety cards MUST override script, dir, and gender.

regions.region: Turkey (Kurmanji), Iraq (Sorani, official in Kurdistan Region), Iran (Sorani/Southern), Syria (Kurmanji)
